title: Early Mathematics Risk in Chinese Kindergartners: Group Differences and Differential Associations of Cognitive, Motivational, and Home Factors
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examined mean‐level group differences and differential associations of cognitive, motivational‐behavioral, and home numeracy factors with early mathematics achievement in 173 Chinese kindergarten children. Covariate‐adjusted group comparisons and moderation analyzes, controlling for age, gender, socioeconomic status, and nonverbal intelligence, compared a sample‐defined Mathematics Risk (MR) group (bottom quartile) with an Average‐Achieving (AA) group (middle 50%). Digit RAN and symbolic comparison showed both significant group differences and Predictor × Group interactions. Working memory and inhibition showed significant interactions without significant group differences. In contrast, task avoidance, social avoidance, formal teaching, and number application differed between groups but showed no significant interactions. Thus, mean‐level differences and differential associations identified partially different correlates of early mathematics risk.
